quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert and cautious. Slow down before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene?

options.text: Keep your focus on driving.
Keep moving forward.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not stop unless you are involved in the accident or emergency help has not yet arrived. Stay focused on your driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accident scenes just to look.

questions.question: How does night driving compare to daytime driving?

options.text: It is less dangerous.
It is equally as dangerous.
It is more dangerous.
It is easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can temporarily blind you. More tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisle next to a handicap parking space?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs usually look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. You will see them on the right side of the road, or on both sides if it is a divided highway.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn after slowing down and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn until the light turns green.
You may turn after you come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic light?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A solid green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it is dangerous.
Traffic moves in opposite directions.
You cannot pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Move to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the chance of a collision. If you drive faster than others, you will keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, stay within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Do not use high beams in fog. Use low beam headlights or fog lights instead.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it is dark and hard to see. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane ends soon.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are going 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: It warns of hazards ahead or nearby.
It alerts you to school zones.
It alerts you to public recreation areas.
It alerts you to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards ahead or nearby. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. Pull off the road safely and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." When does this speed limit start?

options.text: At this sign.
At the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before it begins.
Only during bad weather.

questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign means you must slow down right away. If a new speed limit is shown on this sign, it begins at the sign.

questions.question: You are driving and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Press hard on the brake pedal.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.
Pull over as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and braking lightly. Do not stop on the road. Move to a safe place off the road.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibrations to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibrations to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to alert drowsy or distracted drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you sit in the back seat.
Yes, if you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road or street. You cannot have an open alcohol container in the area where the driver or passengers sit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is cleaning up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that workers may be on or very close to the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance work.
Distance information to nearby locations.

questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about motorist services. These include rest areas, food, gas, hospitals, and other helpful services for drivers.
